title: Tensor compatibility of the hypercohomology-to-sheaf-cohomology edge
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^n$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and K-injective derived global sections $R\Gamma$ [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. Put $A=\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$. For $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$, let $e_K^n:H^nR\Gamma(\mathcal C,K)\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal H^nK)$ send a global cocycle in a K-injective representative to its class in the cohomology sheaf. This map is independent of the representative and natural for every derived morphism $K\to K'$. Use derived tensor, the derived global cup map $c_{K,L}$, and the local tensor-of-cocycles map $\kappa^{a,b}_{K,L}:\mathcal H^aK\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal H^bL\to\mathcal H^{a+b}(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}L)$ of [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product]. For all $K,L\in D(\mathcal O)$, $a,b\geq0$, $x\in H^aR\Gamma K$, and $y\in H^bR\Gamma L$, one has
$$e_{K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L}^{a+b}\bigl(H^{a+b}(c_{K,L})(\kappa^{a,b}_{R\Gamma K,R\Gamma L}(x\otimes y))\bigr)=\Gamma(\kappa^{a,b}_{K,L})(e_K^a(x)\otimes e_L^b(y)).$$
The tensor of global sections on the right is first mapped to the global sections of the sheaf tensor product. No final site object, boundedness, flatness, or quasi-coherence is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BKV (lemma-sheafification-cohomology) and Tag 0FPK (lemma-cup-compatible-with-naive), applied to the global-sections morphism; the edge compatibility is the agent-stated consequence of these cochain descriptions.

proof.text: For any complex $M$, define $\delta_M^n:H^n\Gamma M\to\Gamma\mathcal H^nM$ by sending a compatible family of degree-$n$ cycles to its image under $\ker d_M^n\to\mathcal H^nM$. A global boundary maps to zero, so this is well-defined. For a chain map $v:M\to N$, both $\delta_N^n H^n\Gamma(v)$ and $\Gamma\mathcal H^n(v)\delta_M^n$ send $[z]$ to the family $[v(z)]$. If $v-w=dh+hd$, then on a cycle their difference is $d(hz)$, hence zero on both cohomologies. This is precisely the kernel/quotient description of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]; it uses compatible families, not evaluation at a final object.

source.place: Tag 0BKV, lemma-sheafification-cohomology, proof: kernel/quotient description; global compatible-family version written here

proof.text:
Choose K-injective representatives $I$ for $K$ and $J$ for $L$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], $H^nR\Gamma K=H^n\Gamma I$ (the same termwise K-injective computation in every degree). Set $e_K^n=\delta_I^n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], every derived map between such representatives is represented by a chain map, uniquely up to homotopy; a derived isomorphism between them is a homotopy equivalence. Global sections preserves a chain homotopy termwise, and step 1 is natural for chain maps and unchanged by homotopy. Therefore these maps are independent of the K-injective representative and natural for every derived morphism. More generally, for any complex $P$ and a resolution $r:P\to I$, step 1 gives
$$e_{[P]}^n H^n(\beta_P)=\Gamma(\mathcal H^n(r))\,\delta_P^n,$$
with the canonical identification of $\mathcal H^n[P]$ and $\mathcal H^n I$; here $\beta_P:[\Gamma P]\to R\Gamma[P]$ is induced by $\Gamma(r)$.

source.place: Tag 0BKV, proof, with K-injective representative independence (Derived Categories Tag 070I)

proof.text: Represent $x$ by a global cycle $z\in\Gamma I^a$. It defines a chain map $t:\mathcal O[-a]\to I$, sending $1$ to $z$. The complex $\mathcal O[-a]$ has flat terms and is K-flat: tensoring an acyclic complex with it only shifts that complex, directly from [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Apply [lem-pur-kflat-map-factorization] to obtain a flat-term K-flat $P$, a quasi-isomorphism $r:P\to I$, and $u:\mathcal O[-a]\to P$ with $t\simeq ru$. Put $\widetilde z=u(1)\in\Gamma P^a$. The homotopy equation on $1$ says $z-r(\widetilde z)=d(h(1))$, so $H^a(\beta_P)[\widetilde z]=x$. Similarly construct a flat-term K-flat $Q$, a quasi-isomorphism $s:Q\to J$, and $\widetilde w\in\Gamma Q^b$ mapping to $y$. Thus the replacements retain these particular global cycles; no surjectivity of global sections along an arbitrary resolution is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0G7D, lemma-factor-through-K-flat, including flat terms; explicit application to the two shifted unit maps

proof.text: Put $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{\mathcal O}Q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], $[T]$ is canonically $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L$, and $\rho_{P,Q}$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-naive-cup-comparison] to global sections and $P,Q$. On degree-$(a+b)$ cohomology its left route is the cup product in the question (transported along $[P]\simeq K$, $[Q]\simeq L$); its right route factors through the actual complex $\Gamma T$. Specifically, $\rho_{\Gamma P,\Gamma Q}$ sends the tensor pairing of $[\widetilde z]$ and $[\widetilde w]$ to $[\widetilde z\otimes\widetilde w]$ in the ordinary tensor complex. To verify this even though $\Gamma P,\Gamma Q$ need not be K-flat, take the chain maps $A[-a]\to\Gamma P$ and $A[-b]\to\Gamma Q$ defined by these cycles and apply [lem-sc-module-cup-shifted-unit-tensor]: its single-free-complex normalization gives exactly this summand, with no sign. Naturality of the cocycle pairing of [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product] identifies their images with the given tensor pairing. Consequently the cup product, under $[T]\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L$, is $H^{a+b}(\beta_T)[v]$, where $v$ is the compatible family obtained from $\widetilde z\otimes\widetilde w$ by the $(a,b)$ summand inclusion.

source.place: Tag 0FPK, lemma-cup-compatible-with-naive, global specialization; tensor-of-cocycles normalization from More on Algebra Tag 068G

proof.text: Apply step 2 to $T$: the edge of $H^{a+b}(\beta_T)[v]$ is the global sheaf class $[v]$. On the other hand step 2 applied to $r$ and $s$ identifies $e_K^a(x)$ and $e_L^b(y)$ with the images of the sheaf classes of $\widetilde z$ and $\widetilde w$. On the flat-term K-flat representatives $P,Q$, the definition [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product] sends their tensor to $[\widetilde z\otimes\widetilde w]=[v]$ in $\mathcal H^{a+b}T$. Equality can be checked on each object of the site: both compatible families have precisely that class, and restrictions commute with the summand inclusion. Mapping the tensor of global sections into sections of the sheaf tensor gives exactly this family. Therefore the two sides of the asserted identity are equal. In particular $d(\widetilde z\otimes\widetilde w)=d\widetilde z\otimes\widetilde w+(-1)^a\widetilde z\otimes d\widetilde w=0$; changing either cycle by a boundary changes this class by a boundary, with the sign $(-1)^a$ for a boundary in the second factor.

source.place: Tags 0BKV and 0FPK; final direct equality of the two tensor-cocycle sheaf classes
